environment: RC receiver powered through the VTX, so the RC link was live

observations: Supersedes ...__01, which recorded `fail` for this same run against the earlier procedure. No observation changed: the user scoped this gate to the minimum for safe flight and approved an amendment under which a defect feeding no safety, arming or actuator path, and a fault that fails closed, are recorded rather than gated. __01 is retained; both defects stay open bugs.
Image identity matched the USB gate: ELF 6bdcd149..., binary 16f6e8ed..., clean tree at a921ffe.
Boot was stationary and disarmed. config-show read the baseline before and after the run.
Operator confirmed OSD VBAT and cell voltage consistent with a multimeter at 6 cells, 4.18 V per cell, closing the voltage half of the 2026-07-28 report.
Motors were stopped at boot and did not respond to stick movement while disarmed.
Arming succeeded five times, each through the guarded stop dwell and four-motor eRPM qualification before SYSTEM ARMED. No motor started before that transition.
Arming aborted correctly when throttle was raised during the attempt: 'Arming aborted: throttle exceeds 65'.

Deliberate RC loss while armed stopped the motors immediately: DShot to [0, 0, 0, 0], eRPM zero in the next report. All five 'RC link invalidated by frame timeout' events were operator-initiated. No automatic rearm followed; a fresh ARM-low then ARM-high was needed.
Operator verified motor reaction as expected on roll and pitch, correction opposing the imposed motion, full-stick bounds reached, deadband commanding zero.

The logical-to-physical motor path is byte-identical to pre-conversion 18521d5: MOTOR_OUTPUT_MAP [3, 4, 2, 1], the Quad X mixer, the ferrowasp-core frame conventions, every Foxeer pin and timer. No wiring or airframe change intervened.

Open bug: battery current read a constant 0.1 A with four motors at 6300..7700 eRPM. centiamps = adc_mv * 10000 / 70 / 10 puts raw PC1 near 1 mV, the noise floor, so the fault is upstream of the scale-70 change this candidate adopted for the 2026-07-28 zero-current report.

Open bug: the ESC telemetry manager latched faulted at 207999 ms after one response timeout for logical M4, one miss in 10132, zero CRC failures. Earlier disarms, including the first RC-loss stop, reached zero eRPM unfaulted, so it was not systematic.

Both later arm attempts then aborted on 'ESC idle telemetry qualification timed out', fail-closed. The second followed a battery reconnect, but the latch was set 100 s earlier, so this run does not independently demonstrate the ESC-only power-cycle bug.
After the latch, per-motor eRPM repeated frozen values while DShot commanded [0, 0, 0, 0]: the tracked stale-telemetry item, not turning motors.
Blackbox wrote 1398 pages, zero dropped records, zero write faults. Capture: boot 4, flight 8, pages 17182..18560.

No 'UART4 RX free-buffer pool exhausted on IDLE' warning occurred with the VTX powered, against two in the earlier USB-only run with UART4 floating. The deferred pre-conversion A/B is no longer needed.

Open bug: the first storage-CLI command after each USB port open is rejected once with 'ERR invalid command', then succeeds on retry. CommandParser in crates/ferrowasp-tasks/src/flash_storage.rs never resets its line across port open. Byte-identical to pre-conversion: pre-existing, cosmetic.

Neither carried defect can stop a running motor. Current sense drives only OSD and MSP. EscManager::is_faulted has one consumer, a log line, and internally only suppresses further telemetry requests, so a latch degrades eRPM logging and blocks the next arm; it cannot disarm or disturb actuator output while armed.
limitations: No oscilloscope or logic analyzer: DShot pulse width, jitter, and complementary-output margin were not measured; motor stop is evidenced by the firmware's DShot reports, not at the pins.
Motor identity came from the roll and pitch differential response plus the unchanged output map, not the capped per-motor procedure, which needs a selector image step 1 forbids.
This board has no reset button, so boot-with-ARM-high was exercised as a USB power cycle only.
Yaw was exercised within the stick and correction checks but not logged per motor pair.
Open bug carried past this gate: battery current is uncalibrated at a constant 0.1 A, unusable as a load indication.
Open bug carried past this gate: one telemetry response timeout latches telemetry off until reboot, so a flight after such a latch lacks per-motor eRPM data.
